'''Tanbai''' is the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital capital] of [[Easuhura]], the reigning [[FLLA World Cup]] champions following their victory at the [[1764 FLLA World Cup]] and the eighteenth-largest national economy by nominal [[List of countries by GDP (nominal)|GDP]] in the world. The city had a population of 9,360,000 at the [[Easuhura|Easuhuran]] 1764 census, ranking it the [[List of cities and dependencies by population|fortieth-largest city in the world]] by population. The Easuhuran Federal Museum, located in Tanbai, displays '''The Aldarra''', the permanent trophy of the [[1764 FLLA World Cup]]. [[Easuhura]] previously hosted the [[1660 FLLA World Cup|1660]] and [[1716 FLLA World Cup|1716]] editions of the FLLA World Cup.

==History==

Tanbai's modern prominence dates from the height of the [[Easuhuran Empire]]. Over the course of the 17th century the city rose as the world's principal trading centre, the commercial heart of an empire that at its peak in the 1650s held territory in every corner of the [[World Map|globe]] and ranked among the [[List of largest empires|largest in history]].<ref name="factbook">{{Cite web |title=Easuhura |url=https://www.dia.gov/the-world-factbook/countries/easuhura |website=[[The World Factbook]] |publisher=Deiral Intelligence Agency}}</ref> Its wealth in this period rested on Easuhura's position as a dominant trading nation and on its early industrialisation, the second in the world, a position consolidated during the ''[[Trident accord]]'' between 1595 and 1661.<ref name="factbook" /> Tanbai remained the foremost centre of Easuhuran commerce through the decline that followed the [[Great Imperial War]] and the [[Red War]], and through the global wave of decolonisation that ended most of the empire.

==Geography==

Tanbai lies on the island of [[Italran]], the principal island of the [[Easuhuran Isles]], and is both the capital and the largest city of [[Easuhura]].<ref name="factbook" /> In common with the rest of the country, the city has a [[tropical monsoon]] climate, with warm temperatures and plentiful rainfall throughout the year; local temperatures seldom drop below {{Convert|18|C}} or rise above {{Convert|40|C}}.<ref name="factbook" /> The [[H10 motorway|H10]] orbital motorway encircles the city.

==Demographics==

At the 1764 census Tanbai had a population of 9,360,000, making it by far the largest city in Easuhura, more than three times the size of [[Chayek]], the second-largest, and the [[List of cities and dependencies by population|fortieth-largest city in the world]].<ref name="census">{{Cite web |url=https://www.gov.eas/1765/caX3a/EASUHURA_population_CENSUS.PDF |title=Population Census, 1763 |publisher=[[Census Easuhura]]}}</ref> Residents of the city are known as Tanbaians. As elsewhere in Easuhura, the [[Easuhuran language]] is spoken in the city in a wide variety of dialects and accents.

==Government==

As the national capital, Tanbai is the seat of the central institutions of [[Easuhura]], among them the [[Parliament of Easuhura]] and its lower house, the Home of the Peoples, [[The Central Treasury]], and the [[Bank of Easuhura]], the country's central bank. The city itself is administered as a metropolitan municipality led by the [[Mayor of Tanbai|Mayor]].

==Economy==

Tanbai is one of the largest urban economies in [[Ayuma]] and the second-largest financial centre on the continent. It ranked sixth in the world in the 2025 [[Global Financial Centres Index]].<ref name="gfci">{{Cite web |url=https://www.longfinance-eas.org/gfci/2025 |title=The Global Financial Centres Index, 2025 |website=longfinance-eas.org |publisher=Z/Yen Andah Partnership |date=2025}} Retrieved 1765.</ref> The city is one of the world's leading foreign-exchange markets, handling 22.8 per cent of global turnover in 2022,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bis-andah.org/eas/fx-turnover-survey-2022 |title=Triennial Foreign Exchange Turnover Survey, 2022 |website=bis-andah.org |publisher=Bank for Andah Settlements |date=2022}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and, alongside [[Rivostan]], ranks among the cities most closely integrated with the [[World economy|global economy]], behind [[Tirna]] and [[Fekunza]].

[[Airal's Insurance]], based in Tanbai, is the world's second-largest [[Wikipedia:insurance|insurance]] and [[Wikipedia:reinsurance|reinsurance]] market,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.airalsinsurance.eas/about/global-market |title=Annual Market Report, 1763 |website=airalsinsurance.eas |publisher=[[Airal's Insurance]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1764.</ref> and the advertising group [[Kal-oskin]], one of the largest in the world, is also headquartered in the city. Manufacturing plays a comparatively small role in the local economy: at 3.1 per cent of the workforce, Tanbai has the lowest share of manufacturing employment of any region of Easuhura.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://onsssaw.gov.eas/labour/manufacturing-employment-by-region-1758 |title=Manufacturing Employment by Region, 1758 |website=onsssaw.gov.eas |publisher=Office for National Statistics |date=1758}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

==Transport==

Tanbai stands at the centre of Easuhura's transport network. Its bus system is among the largest in the world, second only to that of [[Bhaliloi]], with more than 5,000 scheduled services each weekday carrying about 6&nbsp;million passengers on over 590 routes.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tanbaibuses.eas/network/route-and-service-data-1763 |title=Tanbai Bus Network Performance Data, 1763 |website=tanbaibuses.eas |publisher=[[Tanbai Buses]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1763.</ref> Of the 1.9&nbsp;billion bus journeys made in Easuhura in 1763, 1.2&nbsp;billion were made in Tanbai,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.passengertransport.org.eas/data/bus-journeys-1763 |title=Annual Bus Passenger Journeys, 1763 |website=passengertransport.org.eas |publisher=[[Easuhura Bus Passenger Association]] |date=1763}} Retrieved 1763.</ref> and the city's [[Double-decker bus|double-decker]] buses, which come in each of the five colours of the Easuhuran flag, are an internationally recognised icon of the city.

The [[Millennium line]], a rail link between Tanbai and [[Paviri]], opened in 1700, and the [[High Speed Rail]] line under construction since 1761 will connect Tanbai with [[Paviri]] and [[Chayek]]. [[Tanbai Kiaodea Airport]], about {{Convert|10|mi|km}} west of the city, handled 43.9&nbsp;million passengers in 1764 and is the world's [[List of busiest airports by passenger traffic|seventh-busiest airport by international passenger traffic]], serving as the hub for the flag carrier [[Easuhuran Airways]] and for [[Strish]]; the smaller [[Tanbai City Airport]] handled a further 13.2&nbsp;million.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.caa.gov.eas/data/airport-rankings-1764 |title=Busiest Easuhuran Airports by Passenger Numbers, 1764 |website=caa.gov.eas |publisher=[[Civil Aviation Authority]] |date=1764}} Retrieved 1764.</ref>

==Culture==

The [[Easuhuran Federal Museum]] in Tanbai holds '''[[The Aldarra]]''', the permanent trophy commissioned for the [[1764 FLLA World Cup]], which [[Easuhura]] won. The city is home to [[Queen's University, Tanbai]].
